edges.description: Persistent perfusion failure injures gray matter neurons and spinal tracts.
edges.target: Anterior horn and spinal tract ischemic injury

edges.description: This node names aortic pathology and perioperative interruption of collateral supply in its own text, so the exposure is the node's own content rather than something acting on it from a distance. Both items are graded to what they actually show: one is a single case in which the interruption was inferred rather than observed, and the other is a series reporting how often the aetiology is aortic surgery.

Dissection, embolism and global hypoperfusion are three routes to the same loss of spinal arterial supply, and all three are named at this node. Graded with the aortic link because the two exposures overlap heavily in their sources and are distinguished more by clinical setting than by mechanism.

edges.description: A rare embolic route to the same node, and it earns its own edge rather than being folded into the embolism exposure because it is the one mechanism that operates in patients with no conventional vascular risk factors. Graded partial because the cited sentence is a recommendation about differential diagnosis rather than a measurement of how often the mechanism occurs.

nodes.description: Aortic disease, aortic dissection, cross-clamping, open aortic repair, and endovascular aneurysm repair can interrupt collateral spinal cord blood supply and precipitate ischemia.

evidence.reference_title: Anterior spinal artery syndrome after infrarenal abdominal aortic surgery.
evidence.snippet: Complete paraplegia due to ischemic spinal cord injury was thought to be caused by interruption of critical collateral blood supply to the spinal cord.

evidence.snippet: there were cases associated with aortic surgery (25%), systemic arteriosclerosis (19.4%) and acute deficit of perfusion (11.1%).

nodes.description: Aortic pathology, vertebral or aortic dissection, arteriosclerosis, embolism, systemic hypotension, perioperative interruption of collateral supply, or rarer embolic mechanisms can reduce spinal cord perfusion and initiate hypoxic-ischemic injury.

evidence.reference_title: Spinal cord ischemia: aetiology, clinical syndromes and imaging features.
evidence.snippet: Aetiologies of infarcts were arteriosclerosis of the aorta and vertebral arteries (23.6%), aortic surgery or interventional aneurysm repair (11%) and aortic and vertebral artery dissection (11%), and in 23.6%, aetiology remained unclear.
